rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes mercy as the through-line of Maryam and notes guidance occurs 17 times in Al-A'raf, 8 in Al-Isra, and 6 in Al-Kahf, linking the greater frequency to an added yāʾ.
rows.anchor: سورة مريم فيها الرحمة من أولها إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presence or absence of أبداً does not determine whether punishment is eternal or leave room for forgiveness; many verses state خالدين فيها alone.
rows.anchor: آيات كثيرة فيها خالدين وحدها وليس في العقيدة أنهم يغفر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبداً is used for the future without a specified duration, while قط is for the past; saying ما رأيته أبداً is a common linguistic error.
rows.anchor: للمستقبل وخطأ أن نقول ما رأيته أبداً وهذا خطأ لغوي شائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulm means exceeding bounds and ranges in degree up to kufr; kufr itself means leaving the faith.
rows.anchor: المعروف أن الظلم هو مجاوزة الحد والكفر هو الخروج عن الملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq means leaving obedience to God; the word is likened to a date that comes out of its husk.
rows.anchor: الفسق هو الخروج عن طاعة الله تعالى وله مراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulm commonly involves violating others' rights, whereas fisq is broader: every oppressor is a fasiq, but a fasiq may only wrong himself.
rows.anchor: الظلم أخذ حقوق الغير والفسق عام، وكل ظالم فاسق وليس كل فاسق ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq has degrees and can reach kufr, as with Iblis; the Qur'an also calls disbelievers fasiqin, while some fisq does not reach disbelief.
rows.anchor: الفسق درجات أيضا وله مراتب حتى يصل إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq can describe wrongdoing that is not disbelief, as in the prohibition of indecency and quarrelling during pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: فيه كفر (الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَّعْلُومَاتٌ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an does not use a present-tense form of جاء; it uses أتى for the corresponding present meaning, so present forms are not part of the comparison.
rows.anchor: القرآن لم يستعمل مضارعا للفعل (جاء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At 9:70, أتتهم رسلهم is the sole such Qur'anic expression; other passages use جاءتهم, which Samarrai says describe harder circumstances, beginning with Al-A'raf.
rows.anchor: وهو الموطن الوحيد الذي جاء فيه نحو هذا التعبير في القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ornament belongs to the earth and what grows on it; flowers and other beauty delight viewers, as God's adornment of the sky does.
rows.anchor: فالزينة هي للأرض والله تعالى قال (حَتَّىَ إِذَا أَخَذَتِ

words: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا
rows.speaker: المستشرقون
rows.claim: The orientalists criticize the Qur'anic account of Moses and argue that humans and jinn together could produce something like the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: حاول المستشرقون أن ينتقدوا القصة في القرآن الكريم فقالوا إنه في قصة موسى

words: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai rejects the inference: one scene can be worded in different ways, but they differ in eloquence; even the three-verse Kawthar cannot be matched.
rows.anchor: لكنهم جهلوا أن القصة الواحدة في القرآن قد يعبر عنها بصور مختلفة

words: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic dialogue is an exact artistic rendering of what Moses, Abraham, and other prophets said, including Moses' speech difficulty noted by Pharaoh and his request for Aaron's eloquence.
rows.anchor: وهي ترجمة دقيقة لما قاله موسى وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Al-Nahl, delay is already the context, and wrongdoers especially wish for more time; this suits placing يستأخرون before يستقدمون.
rows.anchor: فناسب تأخير الأجل في هذه الآية تقديم "يستأخرون"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Al-Hijr, the mockers ask for angels whose descent would bring destruction; the order first mentions overtaking the appointed term to reflect their demand to hasten it.
rows.anchor: فكأنهم عندما طلبوا إنزال الملائكة أرادوا استعجال أجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context is a major clue to meaning: “Taste, you are the mighty, noble one” sounds like praise alone, but in context it is condemnation.
rows.anchor: إذا أخذت من سياقها تظهر وكأنها مدحا بينما في الواقع هي في معرض الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai explains سلك as passing along a path and says it can also mean entering, citing the bee's commanded paths and the question about entering Saqar.
rows.anchor: سلك هو النفاذ في الطريق كما قال تعالى (فاسلكي سبل ربك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud's wording about carrying fits an ark that bears its passengers; in Al-Mu'minun, where no carrying image is given, سلك aptly describes entering the ark first.
rows.anchor: في سورة هود ذكر ما دل على الحمل لأن الحمل جاري في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd's personal confrontation and threat of harm make “the One who originated me” apt: the one who created him will protect him; the following verse also says God can replace the people.
rows.anchor: فالأمر إذن شخصي وليس عامّاً فاقتضى ذكر (الذي فطرني)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq can mean forming or shaping and can describe either origination or representation; fatr means beginning something and belongs specifically to God.
rows.anchor: قد يستعمله البشر بمعنى التصوير مثلاً وهو لفظ عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate pronoun هو may add emphasis and restriction to the statement that God is the Lord of Jesus and his people.
rows.anchor: احتمال أن يكون ضمير منفصل يفيد التوكيد والحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zukhruf addresses people treating Jesus as a deity, so the exclusive wording denies that; Maryam's statement follows the birth and is not in that context.
rows.anchor: السياق في الزخرف جاء في مقام عبادة عيسى واتخاذه إلها

words: مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai proposes a Qur'anic pattern in tasbih verses: when ما is repeated, the following discussion concerns the people of earth; without repetition it concerns something else.
rows.anchor: فالكلام بعدها يكون على أهل الأرض. وإذا لم يكرر (ما) فالكلام ليس على أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Shu'ayb forbearing and rightly guided is ironic praise: his people mean the opposite, as in the taunt in 44:49; context reveals the mockery.
rows.anchor: هو في الأصل مدح لكن إن وضعناه في سياق الآيات فهي استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaygh is deviation to either side; taghyan is exceeding the limit or looking beyond what is permitted.
rows.anchor: زاغ من الزيغان وهو الذهاب يمينا وشمالا أما الطغيان فهو مجاوزة الحد والقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the Prophet's journey, his gaze neither wandered nor exceeded its assigned place despite the scene's pull, praising his restraint in heaven as on earth.
rows.anchor: في رحلته ما مال بصره ولا جاوز قدره بل وقف في المكان الذي خصص له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive مِن means he saw some of God's great signs, not all; the unspecified object magnifies the honor, and the sūra as a whole honors the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لم يرى كل شيء لكن الرحلة كان لها

rows.speaker: الشيخ الشعراوي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrawi's reflection is that the Prophet saw the greatest sign; Samarrai adds that God knows best.
rows.anchor: الشيخ الشعراوي رحمه الله فهو في خواطره يرى أن الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' shirt bearing false blood remains intact; “preyed on him” would imply torn clothes, so Samarrai notes the wording “ate him” instead.
rows.anchor: والافتراس يفترض أن يمزق ثيابه كلها وإخوة يوسف جاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The normally pleasant word “give good news” is used sarcastically for the hypocrites, as in the taunting address in 44:49.
rows.anchor: المعروف أن التبشير بالشيء الحسن أما هنا فجاء التبشير من باب السخرية والتهكم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative ديناً functions as specification by way of praise.
rows.anchor: النصب يدخل في باب التخصيص بالمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed parsing understands the phrase as “without visible pillars,” taking the pillars to exist but remain unseen.
rows.anchor: قسم يقول إنها عمد غير مرئية بمعنى (بغير عمد مرئية)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing stops after “without pillars” and takes ترونها to resume the clause: you see the heavens raised without pillars; Samarrai says both remain possible.
rows.anchor: بغير عمد ثم استأنف ترونها بمعنى ترونها مرفوعة بغير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shorter اسطاعوا is used for the quicker, easier climb; full استطاعوا marks the more demanding, longer work of boring through the barrier.
rows.anchor: استطاعوا تحتاج إلى جهد لنقب السد أما اسطاعوا فهي للصعود على ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blood-stained shirt was fabricated evidence for the brothers' claim that a wolf had eaten Joseph.
rows.anchor: هذه بينة مزورة وليست بيّنة صحيحة (بدم كذب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second use of the shirt is valid evidence of Joseph's innocence when the witness reasons from where it was torn.
rows.anchor: واستعمله مرة أخرى بينة صحيحة للوصول إلى براءة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third shirt is valid evidence that Joseph is alive and brings glad tidings to Jacob; the shirt's arrival is linked to his recovered sight.
rows.anchor: والبينة الثالثة استعمل بينة صحيحة للدلالة على أن يوسف لا يزال حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt that carries the scent need not be the same shirt as the first one; Jacob recognizes his son's smell.
rows.anchor: ليس بالضرورة أنه القميص الأول لكن يعقوب عليه السلام يعرف رائحة ابنه
